title: TKT Module 1 · Additional Practice Test (20 questions)
source: Teacher-created practice based on the supplied Cambridge TKT sample papers

questions.text: In “They have lived here for five years”, what is the main use of the present perfect?
options: To describe a situation that began in the past and continues now
To describe a repeated future arrangement
To describe a finished action at a definite past time

questions.text: Which word is a preposition in “The keys are under the newspaper”?
Which word contains a negative prefix?
Which is a compound noun?
Which pair is a common verb + noun collocation?
In “She speaks remarkably clearly”, what does “remarkably” modify?
Which sentence contains a defining relative clause?
options: My brother, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse.
It was raining, which surprised us.
The book that you lent me is excellent.

questions.text: Which word is the object pronoun?
Which sentence uses “will” to make a prediction based on an opinion?
options: I think the team will win tonight.
She is meeting the manager at six.
Look at those clouds; it is going to rain.

questions.text: Which is a minimal pair?
What is the usual word stress in “photography”?
Which is a voiced consonant sound?
Which sentence is a first conditional?
options: If I had more time, I would travel.
If it rains, we will stay inside.
If she had studied, she would have passed.

questions.text: What is the function of “Would you mind closing the window?”
Which is an example of a lexical set?
A learner says “I goed to the market.” Which error is this?
Which is a receptive skill?
What does “bilingual” mean?
options: learning a language for the first time

questions.text: Which word is a demonstrative pronoun in “Those are mine”?
In “Could you give me a hand?”, what does the phrase mean?

title: TKT Module 2 · Additional Practice Test (20 questions)
source: Teacher-created practice based on the supplied Cambridge TKT sample papers

questions.text: A teacher asks learners to read a short article quickly and choose its best title. What is the main reading subskill?
Learners listen to a train announcement to write down the platform number. What is the main subskill?
At the start of a lesson, learners brainstorm words connected with “holidays”. What is the main aim?
Learners compare two pictures and find ten differences. Which speaking skill is practised most?
Which activity focuses on accurate letter formation?
options: writing a review for a website

questions.text: A lesson plan says learners will “understand the past simple”. What would make this aim more useful?
options: Learners will use regular past forms to describe a finished weekend.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a warmer?
options: to introduce a brief engaging start and focus learners

questions.text: Learners predict an article’s content from its headline and photograph. What are they using?
Which resource is most suitable for showing how a word is pronounced?
Why might a teacher use realia in a lesson on food?
Learners choose the correct verb form from options in a sentence. What kind of practice is this?
Learners role-play ordering food using their own ideas. What kind of practice is this?
Which is a suitable lesson aim for practising skimming?
options: Learners will copy every sentence accurately.
Learners will identify the main idea of a text quickly.

questions.text: Why include an answer key with a self-study worksheet?
options: so learners do not need to read instructions
so learners can check their own work
so the worksheet has more questions

questions.text: Learners put mixed-up sentences into a logical order. What are they focusing on?
A teacher elicits examples before explaining a grammar rule. What approach is this?
Which is the best way to check instructions before a pair task?
options: ask a learner to explain what they will do

questions.text: A teacher plans a backup activity in case a task finishes early. This is an example of:
Learners listen to a dialogue and complete missing words. What is the main focus?
Which activity best practises proofreading?
options: learners find and correct errors in a draft
learners listen for the main idea

title: TKT Module 3 · M3 V62 Full Test (80 questions)
source: User-provided M3 V62 PDF; all 80 questions adapted to interactive format and answers checked against the paper content

questions.text: Teacher classroom language function: “That’s right, he’s wearing a jacket. Are jackets normally long or short?”
Teacher classroom language function: “Then the three friends woke up and continued their journey.”
Teacher classroom language function: “You like that picture. Can you tell your partner why you like it?”
Teacher classroom language function: “Stop writing now and pass your paper to the person on your left.”
Teacher classroom language function: “A quarter past three is the same as three fifteen.”
Teacher classroom language function: “What clothes do you normally only wear in cold weather? Any suggestions?”
A teacher asks learners to look at a text after a short pre-reading task. Which is NOT appropriate?
options: Read carefully and tell me the gist.
Check whether your predictions were correct.
Read quickly and choose the best title.

questions.text: A teacher uses a picture to interest elementary learners in a topic. Which suggestion is NOT appropriate?
options: Say where you think the picture is.
Speculate about what the people have been doing.

questions.text: A pre-intermediate learner asks if she can express a sentence another way. Which response is NOT appropriate?
options: It is highly unlikely anyone would express it that way.
It will not be very clear what you mean.
You can, but it sounds too formal.

questions.text: A teacher checks whether learners remember “safe”. Which question is NOT appropriate?
options: Give a word opposite in meaning to safe.
Where did we see safe yesterday?
You have all seen safe before. Do you understand it?

questions.text: Learners write a complaint to a bank manager. Which advice is NOT appropriate?
options: Check paragraphs and linking words in the final draft.
Register is unimportant if the complaint is clear.
Focus on communicating the complaint in the first draft.

questions.text: Learners struggle to say “atmosphere”. Which support is NOT appropriate?
options: Listen and identify the word stress.
Notice that ph is pronounced /f/, as in enough.
Guess how to spell the word because it is difficult.

questions.text: A teacher focuses on vocabulary learners will meet in a text. Which is NOT an appropriate activity?
options: Match words in the text to meanings below.
Underline unknown words and check whether context or a partner helps.

questions.text: Teacher activity: Focus learners on the topic before they listen to an interview.
Teacher activity: Check that learners understand grammar points during a presentation.
Teacher activity: Get learners to share ideas before a speaking activity.
Teacher activity: Check learners are following the instructions given.
Teacher activity: Help learners understand key words before they read a text.
Teacher activity: Observe learners so you can give feedback after a speaking activity.
Type of writing error: “I like to introduce my town to you.”
Type of writing error: “the huge park in centre”
Type of writing error: “for most of the year, so everybody ...” (the missing comma after year)
Type of writing error: “some of children’s games”
Type of writing error: “its nice that ice-cream is available”
Type of writing error: “the park authoritys”
Type of writing error: “Now I’m to busy to go to the park”
Function of learner language: “We are going to write a description, right? But now we have to just talk and brainstorm ideas.”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of learner language: “We could use headings, like buildings, shops, restaurants and sightseeing.”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of learner language: “Are we supposed to talk about our home town or the town we study in?”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of learner language: “The teacher said we could choose, but I think the town we study in, so we can all contribute.”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of learner language: “Actually, I think it would be better to talk about our home towns. We would have more to say.”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of learner language: “Umm, I suppose so. We’ll talk about our home towns.”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of learner language: “What are the main attractions in your town, Suzanne?”
options: C. Giving yourself time to think
E. Interrupting to make a point

questions.text: Function of written learner language: “As you know, we are having a party for Martin on Saturday, at my house in the garden.”
Function of written learner language: “It would be a good idea to bring a sweater.”
Function of written learner language: “We can go shopping, decorate the house and then prepare the food.”
Function of written learner language: “That rice dish is delicious; I expect everyone will love it.”
Function of written learner language: “We will not have enough plates, but we can buy paper ones.”
Function of written learner language: “I have lots of CDs. Is that enough, do you think? Mark is bringing music too.”
Function of written learner language: “What time does your gym lesson finish on Saturday?”
Why can a quiet period in a lesson be useful? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: A change of pace can help learning.
Learners need quiet time to consolidate learning.
The teacher can prepare the next activity.

questions.text: Are definitions always the best way to explain vocabulary? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: They can be more complex than the word.
Learners can be encouraged to write their own definitions.

questions.text: Why should learners personalise new language? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: They remember language when it relates to real life.

questions.text: Why should teachers learn about their learners? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: To be aware of sensitive areas.
To discuss personal issues in class.

questions.text: Should feedback be given after every task? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: Feedback can make the task more meaningful.
Go through answers even when you know they are correct.
Feedback can give learners a sense of progress.

questions.text: Do teachers need to follow everything in a lesson plan? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: An activity may no longer be necessary.
Learners may find controlled practice boring.

questions.text: Why vary the tone and speed of your voice? Choose the trainee response that is NOT appropriate.
options: It prevents learners becoming bored and stopping listening.
It makes it easier for learners to copy you.
Changes in voice can support meaning.

questions.text: Classroom management response: Some learners find it difficult to speak in front of the whole class.

questions.text: Teacher role: After class, the teacher talks to individual learners about their progress.
Teacher role: While monitoring pair work, the teacher explains why she agrees with learners’ opinions.
Teacher role: The teacher stops controlled practice when learners start using L1.
Teacher role: The teacher asks a learner to repeat the instructions.
Teacher role: The teacher invites learners to ask for his views in a discussion.
Teacher role: The teacher checks that noisy groups do not distract others.
Teacher role: The teacher brings photocopied news articles to class.
Purpose of interaction pattern: Learners individually brainstorm words for city and countryside.
options: C. Build confidence in functional language

questions.text: Purpose of interaction pattern: The class chorally drills advice structures before a role-play.
options: C. Build confidence in functional language

questions.text: Purpose of interaction pattern: The class brainstorms vocabulary for describing people before describing family photos.
options: C. Build confidence in functional language

questions.text: Purpose of interaction pattern: Learners show written work to a partner and discuss it before handing it in.
options: C. Build confidence in functional language

questions.text: Purpose of interaction pattern: Two teams compete in a quiz on job vocabulary.
options: C. Build confidence in functional language

questions.text: Purpose of interaction pattern: The teacher uses many mingling activities in the first lessons with a new class.
options: C. Build confidence in functional language

questions.text: Correction strategy: The teacher uses fingers to show where a mistake was made.
Correction strategy: The teacher drills words containing the target sounds.
Correction strategy: The teacher notes errors in a role-play and explains what was wrong and why in the next lesson.
Correction strategy: The teacher uses a correction code on essays.
Correction strategy: The teacher draws a timeline and reminds a learner not to use present perfect with past-time expressions.
Correction strategy: The teacher echoes “I’ll give it to him when I will see him!” to prompt correction.
Feedback focus: “Include a strong opening and link ideas together more.”
Feedback focus: “A well-balanced argument; remember to allow time to check your work.”
Feedback focus: “Good use of adverbs such as however to link paragraphs.”
Feedback focus: “Try not to use the same adjectives too often.”
Feedback focus: “Your handwriting is getting easier to read.”
Feedback focus: “Use synonyms to avoid repeating the same words.”
Feedback focus: “Use the irregular verb list to check your work.”
